evidence: Current preflight resolves command.cwd and validates package.json there.
Current packageScriptName assumes argv[1] is the npm-compatible command and therefore skips script validation when a package-selection option precedes the command.
The command runner executes the original argv unchanged, so npm package-selection options can make execution target a package different from the manifest preflighted at cwd.

<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | CONFIRMED |
| Confidence | HIGH |
| Severity | MEDIUM |
| Task Type | Correctness / verification preflight |
| Complexity | STANDARD |

### What Was Claimed

The issue reports that npm package-selection flags are accepted by the tracked verification command but the preflight validates the wrong `package.json`.

### What We Found

The claim is reproducible from the current tree. `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` resolves and validates `command.cwd`, while `forge_verify` executes the complete bound `argv` unchanged. `packageScriptName` only treats `argv[1]` as the package-manager command. An option such as `npm --prefix web test` therefore skips script validation entirely; when a selection option appears after the command, any script validation still inspects `cwd` even though npm may execute the selected package.

### Root Cause

Package selection is represented in two independent inputs (`cwd` and package-manager flags) without an invariant that they identify the same package. The preflight has no guard for npm package-location/workspace-selection options and does not parse harmless options before locating the script command. The documented and safe model is to select the package solely with the bound repository-relative `cwd`.

### Affected Files

| Path | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Detect package-manager package-selection options, locate commands beyond harmless flags, and fail closed instead of validating a potentially different manifest. |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Add regression coverage for npm package-location/workspace flags and the valid `cwd`-selected package path. |

### Evidence

- `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` calls `resolveVerificationCommandDirectory` for `command.cwd` and then `assertPackageScript` against `${cwd}/package.json`.
- `packageScriptName` currently reads only `argv[1]`; `npm --prefix web test` returns no script name and receives no manifest check.
- `forge_verify` destructures `[program, ...args]` and runs those args with the resolved `command.cwd`, preserving any package-selection flags.
- The repository README says monorepo commands must bind `cwd` to the package that owns the script and recommends CI-only verification when no local command is configured.

### History Findings

- The issue body identifies source PR #110, finding `correctness-001`, and reviewed head `3503e27b5ddaf401411e9fe8c4d35beac0f5c95f`.
- The supplied finding evidence says commit `d174f8e9d8ff88c1a40b8a75c99489c76ef52e92` addressed the prior round by rejecting npm package-location options and requiring `workingDirectory`.
- The current integration tree retains the `cwd` contract but has no corresponding package-selection rejection, so the remediation is not complete on this base.

### Recommendation

Keep package selection deterministic: reject npm package-location/workspace-selection flags in tracked verification argv and direct operators to set the repository-relative `cwd`. Parse supported package-manager commands past harmless options so script preflight remains active when ordinary flags precede the command. Add focused regression tests for prefix/workspace forms and the valid cwd-based invocation.

### Related Issues

- #94 (source issue referenced by the review finding)
- #110 (source pull request)
- #111 (current remediation)

### Decomposition Assessment

**Required**: no — the root cause and regression surface are confined to verification preflight and its adapter tests.

<!-- FORGE:FAST_PATH -->

**Complexity**: STANDARD  
**Task type**: CORRECTNESS / VERIFICATION PREFLIGHT

- No phases skipped.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Reject npm package-location and workspace-selection flags rather than preflighting a potentially different package.
- [ ] Preserve the `cwd`-selected package as the sole package manifest authority.
- [ ] Continue recognizing package scripts when harmless npm options precede the command.
- [ ] Add focused regression coverage for rejected flags and the valid monorepo `cwd` path.

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective

Make verification preflight fail closed when npm argv selects a package independently of the configured repository-relative `cwd`, so the manifest preflighted is always the manifest used by the verification command.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts`
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change `.forge/config.json`, the verification policy schema, or the `cwd` field contract.
- Do not execute verification commands during preflight or add shell/process behavior.
- Do not resolve package-selection flags to arbitrary paths or permit a second package authority.
- Do not change GitHub workflows, review policy, branch policy, UI, or unrelated adapters.
- Do not add dependencies or modify generated/runtime artifacts.

### Invariants

- Required commands only are preflighted, as today.
- Every package script check is against the canonical package directory selected by `command.cwd`.
- npm package-location and workspace-selection options are rejected with a policy-path error directing operators to configure `cwd`.
- `--` terminates npm option inspection so script arguments are not mistaken for package selection.
- Existing executable, repository-boundary, symlink, JSON, and package-script checks retain their fail-closed behavior.

### Deliverables

- A deterministic npm package-selection option guard in `verification-preflight.ts`.
- Focused regression coverage for prefix/workspace selection forms, option placement, delimiter behavior, and valid cwd-based monorepo verification.
- A committed implementation that passes the tracked `check` command.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| INV-1 | Detect npm `--prefix`, `--workspace`/`-w`, `--workspaces`, and workspace-root/package-location variants before manifest validation. |
| INV-2 | Report `${configPath} verification.commands.<name>.argv` and require package selection through the already validated `cwd`. |
| INV-3 | Keep package script detection and manifest validation rooted at the canonical `cwd`; preserve harmless command forms. |
| INV-4 | Add adapter tests proving unsafe selection flags fail and `cwd: "web"` succeeds. |
| INV-5 | Run `forge_verify({ name: "check" })` after implementation commit preparation and record its result. |

### Out of Scope

- Supporting npm workspace/prefix execution by separately preflighting selected manifests.
- Changing pnpm, yarn, or bun command semantics beyond shared behavior unaffected by the npm guard.
- Runtime verification execution, CI configuration, merge, issue closure, or cleanup.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### Relevant History

- Issue #111 is a correctness finding from PR #110, with source issue #94 and reviewed head `3503e27b5ddaf401411e9fe8c4d35beac0f5c95f`.
- The supplied finding evidence names `d174f8e9d8ff88c1a40b8a75c99489c76ef52e92` as a prior round remediation that rejected npm package-location options and required a working directory.
- The current tree documents monorepo `cwd` ownership in `README.md`, and `parseForgePolicy` normalizes/restricts it to a repository-relative path.

### Callers and Data Flow

- `workflows/work-on.ts` invokes `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` before launching implementation.
- `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` canonicalizes the worktree root, resolves each required command's `cwd`, checks executable availability, then checks the package script.
- `agents/child-runtime.ts` later runs the exact bound argv with the same resolved command cwd through `forge_verify`.
- Because argv remains unchanged, a package-selection flag can redirect npm while the current preflight reads a different manifest.

### CI Surface

- `.forge/config.json` defines required `check` as `npm run check` with `cwd: "."`.
- `package.json` defines `check`, `typecheck`, and `test`; the tracked local check is the authoritative local readiness command.
- GitHub CI remains parent-owned and is evaluated after PR preparation on the reviewed head.

### Prior Findings

- The review finding specifically identifies package-selection flags as parsed but mismatched with the manifest preflight.
- The repository guidance requires regression tests for safety/recovery fixes and says monorepo commands must bind `cwd` to the owning package.

### Hazards

- Rejecting too few npm aliases could leave a second package selector active.
- Rejecting flags after the command but before `--` is necessary because npm accepts option placement beyond argv[1].
- Flags after `--` are script arguments and must not be rejected as npm package selection.
- Error text must identify the tracked policy argv path and provide an actionable `cwd` remediation without exposing or executing untrusted paths.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Add a small npm-specific package-selection detector that recognizes exact and `=value` forms of package-location/workspace-selection options, plus short workspace/global aliases, and stops at `--`. (INV-1, INV-2)
2. Invoke the detector after executable validation and before `packageScriptName`; throw `VerificationPreflightError` at the tracked argv path with a `cwd` remediation. (INV-2, INV-3)
3. Preserve existing manifest/path checks and add focused fixture assertions for prefix, workspace, workspace-root, and delimiter cases; retain the valid `web` cwd case. (INV-3, INV-4)
4. Inspect the bounded diff, run the required named `check`, and commit only the two allowed files. (INV-5)

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
